questions.corrige_markdown:
$\sim q$ (not $q$) takes the opposite truth value to $q$.

$p\wedge\sim q$ ($p$ and not $q$) is true only when $p$ is true AND $\sim q$ is true.

| $p$ | $q$ | $\sim q$ | $p\wedge\sim q$ |
|---|---|---|---|
| T | T | F | F |
| T | F | T | T |
| F | T | F | F |
| F | F | T | F |

Row by row: (T, T): $\sim q=$ F, so T and F gives F. (T, F): $\sim q=$ T, so T and T gives T. (F, T): $\sim q=$ F, so F. (F, F): $\sim q=$ T, but $p$ is F, so F.
